A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPROD research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original SPROD evaluations on five spurious-OOD benchmarks, non-spurious OOD experiments, backbone comparisons, and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds evaluated baselines and conventional OOD benchmark results.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain normalized class prototypes, classification-based subgroup construction, one reassignment/refinement step, and nearest-prototype scoring. SPROD-KMeans and SPROD-Converged already appeared in v1's appendix; their appearance in v2 does not introduce new method components.

E1.justification: v2 adds conventional OOD evaluation using CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and full ImageNet-1k, each with near- and far-OOD settings (Table 3). This substantially extends coverage beyond the retained five spurious-OOD benchmarks and their existing SVHN, LSUN, and iSUN evaluations.

E2.justification: The ResNet-50 comparison in Table 2 expands from 11 to 19 baselines by evaluating GEN, ASH, NECO, NNGuide, Relation, SCALE, fDBD, and NCI. The existing CLIP comparisons are retained through relocation from v1 Appendix A.1 to v2 Appendix C.

E3.justification: The added conventional evaluation adopts the stated OpenOOD protocol, separates near- and far-OOD AUROC, and reports an average across six settings. Existing spurious-correlation levels, dataset constructions, backbone settings, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged; the PDFs do not document retuning the retained experiments.

E4.justification: Figure 4 revises one result in the fine-tuning/correlation analysis: frozen ResNet-18 KNN at 90% correlation falls from approximately 98.6 to 93.9 plotted AUROC. The scoring, low-shot, stage, and prototype-variant analyses otherwise retain their questions and evidence, including the relocated appendix studies.

E5.justification: Both versions state five repetitions with different random seeds and mean/standard-deviation reporting. No new significance testing or uncertainty-estimation procedure is introduced. Revised standard-deviation values in Table 2 are result changes rather than changes in statistical practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds conventional benchmark results and eight baselines' SP-OOD results. ASH now leads Spurious ImageNet AUROC at 86.6 versus SPROD's 85.3. Under the retained AnimalsMetaCoCo/ResNet-50 setting, SPROD's reported AUROC changes from 82.1 to 82.4 and FPR@95 from 70.1 to 69.5; Table 2 averages change from 85.0/49.1 to 85.1/49.0. Several reported standard deviations also change, while most appendix results remain identical.

T1.justification: New Appendix A introduces orthogonal core, spurious, and irrelevant feature subspaces; binary-class distributional assumptions; group and OOD definitions; and expected-distance derivations explaining prototype bias and its proposed removal. v1 contains method equations but no corresponding formal theoretical analysis.

C1.justification: The introduction adds theoretical insight into spurious-bias mitigation as an explicit contribution. The central claims about the post-hoc method, unknown spurious correlations, annotation and tuning requirements, sample efficiency, and AnimalsMetaCoCo remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 6 newly acknowledges that SPROD is not best on every metric or setting, especially conventional OOD, and interprets this through robustness/performance tradeoffs. Existing limitations involving class-label dependence and the mismatch with some Spurious ImageNet features are retained.

D1.justification: v1 Appendix G links anonymous code and promises the cleaned AnimalsMetaCoCo dataset after acceptance. v2 Appendix I reports both code and data as available through a named repository. The GPU and OpenOOD implementation disclosures remain unchanged; repository availability is reported by the PDF, not independently verified.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands coverage of recent post-hoc detectors and explicitly positions SPROD against prototype approaches including CIDER, PALM, and PROWL. PALM was already cited in v1's appendix. Additional generative-classification literature strengthens the positioning in Section 3.2; these changes exceed bibliographic renumbering.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose edits, expands related-work explanations, moves the zero-shot comparison later in Results, and reorganizes the appendices around new Appendix A and a separate comparison appendix. The main narrative and most existing exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains baseline rows, and new Table 3 presents conventional benchmarks. Figure 4 uses wider panels with vertically arranged backbone groups, and Figure 3 adds an SP-OOD legend entry. Most other figures and tables retain their displays, with relocation or resizing.

improvement.justification: The expanded comparisons and conventional benchmarks better support general applicability, while the reported dataset release improves reproducibility relative to v1. These gains are tempered by problems in the new theory: Appendix A.0.7 omits spurious variance from ID distances without a zero-variance assumption. Numerical inconsistencies also remain, including Section 5.3 reporting 49.1 FPR@95 where Table 2 reports 49.0. The net gain is therefore clearer in empirical coverage and accessibility than in theoretical rigor.
